lifecycle_definitions.validated_preserved: Rule has cleared its breadth/material gate at least twice (or once on a multi-shape harness backed by prior single-shape passes) and is now treated as known-good. Its range/bucket/candidate_count must NOT be edited; its workloads remain in the harness for regression detection only. Mandatory gate per iteration: regression_guard. The full breadth/material gate is REPORTED ALONGSIDE but does not block iteration success.
lifecycle_definitions.validate_active: Rule is under active validation. Mandatory gate per iteration: the rule's breadth/material gate. Failing the gate is iteration failure for this rule and triggers iter-N+1 investigation.
lifecycle_definitions.diagnostic: Rule is probed but not gated. Reported alongside; pass/fail does not affect iteration success. Used for early-stage exploration, for validated-but-flaky regimes that need attribution work before promotion, or for active prompt-tightening trials where iteration success should not depend on whether the tightening succeeded. iter-11 used this for attention_d128_short during its tightening trial; iter-12 has no diagnostic policy entry because d128 has been removed.
lifecycle_definitions.removed: iter-12 introduces the conceptual (not JSON-field) state for buckets that have been actively tested across multiple iterations and are now moved to blocked_classes after a failed tightening trial. attention_d128_short transitions to this state in iter-12. Distinguished from never-validated buckets in blocked_classes by full provenance (iter-3..iter-11 perf/time/compile trajectory) recorded in the blocked_classes entry.

directional_gate.description: Weak signal -- worth another iteration but NOT an improvement claim.
directional_gate.interpretation: If only directional_gate passes, run a follow-up iteration; do not claim the heuristic works.

material_gate.description: Required threshold to call a class/group's range guidance real per shared_context materiality.
material_gate.interpretation: Only the material_gate passing constitutes evidence the prompt-only range heuristic improves the first batch. NOTE: the material gate measures whether a heuristic delivers a real improvement on its driven dimension; it does NOT separately enforce that wall-time/compile must not regress when perf is the driving dimension. iter-10/iter-11 d128 passed material_gate via the perf branch (perf<=0.95) but failed the d128_short_replication_gate on wall-time and compile_total. iter-12 retires the d128_short_replication_gate (no policy entry) and replaces it with attention_d128_short_unprompted_sanity for the now-sanity attention_2k_d128 workload.

harness_requirements.description: iter-12 introduces NO new harness or matcher code changes. The matcher already supports buckets with no policy entry as no-guidance (the d64_long pattern since iter-9). attention_2k_d128 will join attention_4k_d64 in receiving no Range-Based Heuristics section. iter-7's p25/p75 per-repeat distribution and iter-8's per-config compile_time and per-batch benchmark_time aggregation are already in place and stay. iter-12 does not add new workloads. The harness retains the same 16-workload set as iter-11 (5 RMS + 6 narrow + 3 mid + 1 attention d128 + 1 attention d64). The headline assignment of attention_2k_d128 changes from main_attention_d128_short to sanity_attention_d128_short_unprompted; the workload itself is the same. iter-13+ may drop one or both attention sanity workloads if their sanities are stable.

Run `scripts/llm_heuristics_autoresearch.py` with arms=[baseline, range_prompt], llm_max_rounds=1, repeats=3, workloads=union(main_workloads, sanity_workloads_list) (16 total), CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2, model=gpt-5-2, autotuner=LLMGuidedSearch, range-heuristics-path=/tmp/helion_heuristics_loop/claude/range_policy_iteration_12.json. decisions_for_iteration_12.validated_preserved_set: Decision: RMS, narrow softmax, mid softmax all preserved as `validated_preserved` for iter-12. RMS now has eight consecutive material/regression reproductions (iter-3 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 11); narrow has seven (iter-5 2-shape, iter-6 6-shape, iter-7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 6-shape); mid has seven (iter-5 single-shape, iter-6 single-shape, iter-7 mandatory 3-shape breadth, iter-8 / 9 / 10 / 11 3-shape regression-guard). All three keep regression guards as the only mandatory gate; their material/breadth gates are reported_alongside. Range/bucket/candidate_count for all three are byte-identical to iter-11. iter-12 watch items: iter-11 mid perf=0.999 stepped DOWN from iter-9/iter-10 1.002 (an improvement -- mid no longer hugs the 1.02 ceiling); iter-11 narrow time=0.635 was the second-best 6-shape result in the 7-iter run; iter-11 RMS time=0.735 sat at the 8-iter mean.
decisions_for_iteration_12.attention_d128_short_decision: Decision: REMOVE attention_d128_short from the active policy list. Move bucket head_dim_bin_in=[`<=128`] AND seq_bin_in=[`<=2048`] to blocked_classes with full iter-3..iter-11 trajectory provenance. Demote attention_2k_d128 from main_workloads to sanity_workloads_list with new attention_d128_short_unprompted_sanity reported-alongside gate (same band as attention_d64_long_unprompted_sanity). NO matcher code change required (the matcher treats no-policy buckets as no-guidance, identical to the d64_long pattern since iter-9).
decisions_for_iteration_12.attention_d128_short_decision_rationale: iter-11 d128 result under tightened policy (candidate_count 4 -> 2, num_warps [4, 8] -> [4]): perf_geo=0.806 (still material 19.4% win, in iter-5..iter-11 band {0.776, 0.781, 0.799, 0.800, 0.806, 0.822, 0.876}), time_geo=1.080 (FAILED gate ceiling 1.02 by 0.060), per-shape median time=1.125 (FAILED 1.05 ceiling by 0.075), max_repeat_time=1.198, compile_total=1.523 (52% slower compile -- MATERIAL per >=20% rule, WORSE than iter-10's 1.250), per-config compile mean=1.444 (44% slower per config). The iter-11 stability classifier put this outcome in PATH B (PARTIAL -- TIME); the iter-11 plan offered 'further tighten' or 'REMOVE'. Per the user's iter-12 brief, no clearly different minimal mechanism is justified. Per-config compile cost being elevated even with two axes already tightened means count and warps were not the compile-cost drivers; the cost is intrinsic to the suggested config space. Further prompt narrowing (l2_groupings -> [16]) is the same mechanism class that has now been tested twice and failed both times. Hard-execution cap or anti_ranges would require code changes or telemetry not currently in scope. REMOVE is the right call: it stops paying the 52% compile cost on every benchmark while preserving the option to revisit if (a) per-config compile-time attribution telemetry identifies a specific compile-cost mechanism in iter-13+, or (b) iter-12 d128 sanity result shows the iter-3..iter-11 perf signal was not actually prompt-attributable (REMOVE costs nothing). Why DEMOTE-only is also not enough: iter-11 already chose lifecycle=diagnostic with the tightening; the result was time=1.080 and compile=1.523. Lifecycle alone does not address the user's wall-time/compile concern -- diagnostic still applies the prompt and pays the compile cost. Why a swap to a sanity workload (not full deletion): preserves the 7-iter perf series for trend-tracking, detects if d64_long sanity behavior is GPU/B200-attention-specific via cross-shape comparison, mirrors d64_long pattern, costs almost nothing.
decisions_for_iteration_12.attention_d128_short_perf_signal_attribu: Open question for iter-12: is the iter-3..iter-11 d128 perf win prompt-attributable, LLM-baseline, or some mix? iter-12 sanity (no prompt) will produce baseline-equivalent attention_2k_d128 results modulo LLM API nondeterminism. If iter-12 d128 sanity perf is in [0.95, 1.05] (the same band as d64 sanity), the perf wins were prompt-attributable; the user accepts losing that 19% perf win in exchange for the wall-time/compile fix. If iter-12 d128 sanity perf is below 0.95 (e.g., 0.85-0.95), the LLM finds strong d128 configs unprompted; the iter-3..iter-11 wins were partially LLM-baseline; the prompt's marginal contribution was smaller than reported. Either way the iter-12 decision (REMOVE) is correct on the user's compile/wall-time objective; the perf attribution question only affects how strong the iter-3..iter-11 prompt signal really was.
decisions_for_iteration_12.attention_d64_long: Decision: continue blocked/no-guidance. iter-9 sanity passed inside [0.90, 1.10] (time_geo=1.028, max=1.086). iter-10 sanity geomean inside band (time_geo=1.032, perf_geo=0.999) but max time slightly past 1.10 in repeat 1 (1.161). iter-11 sanity inside band in ALL THREE repeats (time_geo=0.991, perf_geo=0.991, max=1.050). 3 consecutive in-band sanities -- the d64_long block is empirically permanent. iter-12 continues the same setup. iter-12 expects a 4th consecutive in-band geomean. Keeping d64 sanity in iter-12 (rather than dropping per the iter-11 plan's PATH suggestion) provides cross-shape comparability with the new d128 sanity workload: both should be neutral if REMOVE is working as expected. iter-13+ may drop one or both attention sanity workloads after additional in-band history accumulates.
decisions_for_iteration_12.no_broadening_to_weak_classes: Decision: blocked_classes list is unchanged from iter-11 except for the new attention_d128_short entry. row_norm_layer, row_cross_entropy, matmul family, elementwise, row_softmax_wide, attention_small_short, attention_large_or_long, sum_or_null. No new evidence has accumulated for any of these since iter-3.

Workload count is 16 (5 RMS + 6 narrow + 3 mid + 1 attention d128 + 1 attention d64). The deltas vs iter-11 are: (a) d128_short policy entry deleted, (b) attention_2k_d128 moved from main to sanity, (c) main_attention_d128_short headline group renamed to sanity_attention_d128_short_unprompted, (d) new attention_d128_short_unprompted_sanity gate, (e) attention_d128_short_replication_gate deleted, (f) new blocked_classes entry attention_d128_short, (g) iter-11 evidence rolled into all 3 preserved policy provenance blocks. NO matcher / harness / autotuner code changes.
decisions_for_iteration_12.exact_template_prompt_and_seeds: Both remain disabled. No iter-11 evidence justifies re-enabling them. iter-12's experimental question (does removing d128 leave RMS/narrow/mid as a clean, stable validated set?) does not require any re-enablement.
decisions_for_iteration_12.iter_13_paths_conditional_on_iter_12_out: PATH A (3 mandatory pass; both d128 sanity AND d64 sanity in band): CLEAN STABLE STATE. iter-13 holds the validated set steady (RMS / narrow / mid) and explores ONE incremental probe -- either widen mid_probe to cols=`<=8192` (mid data gap closure if AOT supports) OR drop one sanity workload (d64 has 4 in-band passes; freeing a slot for a new probe). Probe selection driven by AOT data, not by guess. PATH B (3 mandatory pass; d128 sanity in band; d64 sanity time > 1.10): D64 DRIFT. Investigate harness/LLM API drift rather than heuristic. d64 has been in band 3 iters; sudden out-of-band suggests external drift. Roll forward iter-12 JSON unchanged. PATH C (3 mandatory pass; d128 sanity time > 1.10): D128 SANITY DRIFT. The unprompted LLM is producing wall-time-bad configs on this shape (intrinsic d128 attention compile difficulty on B200). Confirms REMOVE was right; no further policy action. PATH D (3 mandatory pass; d128 sanity perf < 0.95): D128 PROMPT WAS NOT THE PERF DRIVER. iter-3..iter-11 perf wins were partially LLM-baseline; the prompt's marginal contribution was smaller than reported. iter-13 marks d128 as permanently REMOVE -- no mechanism work needed. PATH E (3 mandatory pass; d128 sanity perf in [0.95, 1.05] AND time in [0.90, 1.10]): EXPECTED. The iter-3..iter-11 d128 perf wins WERE prompt-attributable. REMOVE means we lose that 19% perf win; the user has accepted that tradeoff for the wall-time/compile objective. iter-13 holds. PATH F (RMS / narrow / mid regression guard fails): REAL REGRESSION. Roll back to iter-11 JSON. Investigate before further iteration. PATH G (Mid softmax perf_geo trends back up to ~1.005): MID PERF DRIFT WATCH. iter-11 mid perf=0.999 was a step DOWN from iter-9/iter-10 1.002. If iter-12 reverts to ~1.005, that's noise. If it climbs above 1.02 (the regression-guard ceiling), that's a real regression and triggers PATH F. PATH H (Both sanities in band for 3+ consecutive iters): DROP BOTH ATTENTION SANITIES at iter-15+ to free 2 workload slots for narrow row expansion (rows>4096) once AOT data is available, or for a new class probe.
decisions_for_iteration_12.harness_telemetry_continuity: iter-8's per-config compile_time and per-batch benchmark_time aggregation, iter-7's p25/p75 per-repeat distribution, and the attention markdown auto-rendering all continue unchanged in iter-12. The d128 sanity specifically benefits from continued compile/benchmark attribution: iter-12 d128 sanity compile_total should be near 1.0 (no prompt = baseline-equivalent). If d128 sanity compile_total is still elevated, the compile cost is intrinsic to the d128 attention configs the LLM finds -- not to any specific prompt -- and there is genuinely nothing for the heuristic loop to do.

agreement_with_codex: Iteration 12 follows the user's iter-12 brief (delivered via direct prompt) and the iter-11 Codex review (`/tmp/helion_heuristics_loop/codex/range_policy_iteration_11_review.md`): (a) preserve RMS / narrow softmax / mid softmax wins byte-identical to iter-11 unless data strongly says otherwise -- data says preserve; iter-11 results passed all 3 regression guards cleanly; (b) treat attention d64 long as blocked / no-guidance after iter-11 sanity result (3rd consecutive in-band) -- iter-12 continues the same setup; (c) for attention d128 short, the user's iter-12 brief explicitly directed REMOVE if no clearly different minimal mechanism is justified, and the iter-11 telemetry rules out the obvious next mechanisms (count and warps were not the compile-cost drivers); selected REMOVE. Codex iter-11 review caveat: 'If compile cost stays elevated, the next iteration should remove d128 or tighten another concrete axis only if telemetry identifies one.' Telemetry did not identify another concrete axis (compile_total went from 1.250 to 1.523 under the tightened policy; per-config compile mean=1.444 means individual configs are slow to compile, not just numerous). REMOVE is the answer per Codex's own iter-11 caveat. (d) keep the next benchmark first-round prompt-only -- yes, no design change. (e) treat small deltas as noise (>=5% perf or >=20% wall-time) -- applied; iter-11 d128 wall-time regression (1.080) is NOT material per the >=20% rule but did fail the 1.02 gate ceiling; compile regression (1.523) IS material per the >=20% rule. (f) Canonical GPU continues at CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2.
